docs.purpose: A panel that slides up from the saved-jobs board when the user taps the search button. They type an address or permit number, and tapping a result claims that job onto their board straight away with a confirming buzz. If the claim fails, a red message appears in the panel and the job is not added.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 2 contracts: `/api/leads/search`, `/api/leads/save`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `entitlements`, `lead_views`, `permits` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `lead_views`. It holds no client-side store, so there is no local copy of server state to keep in sync. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.
docs.under_126: **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the SEARCH renderer (declared debounce, minimum query length, rate bucket and candidate shape), reading by reference: `/api/leads/search`, `/api/leads/save`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `mobile/src/components/feed/SearchPermitsSheet.tsx`.

emits: mobile/src/components/feed/SearchPermitsSheet.tsx:58 — logQueryInvalidate only; no track() call in the file

identity.owner: unassigned (no CODEOWNERS file and no owner registry exists in the repo — measured 2026-09-15)

versioning.why: The search rows are parsed by a Zod mirror that throws to the ErrorBoundary on drift; the route returns a five-field projection that can grow but not shrink.

inputs.why: GET /api/leads/search?q= returns up to 20 permits ordered by last_seen_at; the sheet renders nothing else.

outputs.why: Claiming a permit POSTs /api/leads/save with saved:true and waits for the server before invalidating the flight board — no optimistic insert, because the board grouping is computed server-side.
outputs.rollback: none needed — nothing is written locally before the POST resolves; onError sets an inline claimError and the sheet stays open.

state.why: It owns no store — the query text and the claim error are component state, and the only durable effect is the flight-board cache invalidate.

staleness.why: useSearchPermits declares a 60-second staleTime because search results age quickly; there is no debounce, so the cache is the only thing limiting request volume.

session.why: /api/leads/search is under the authenticated /api/leads prefix and the handler resolves a user context before querying.

rls_class.why: It reads permits, which is RLS-enabled with zero policies (default deny); the claim write lands on the Class-A lead_views table through the save route.

guards.rate_bucket: none on the search itself — src/app/api/leads/search/route.ts calls no withRateLimit; the claim POST uses leads-save:{uid} at 60/min

checks.why: useMutation is not serialised, so a rapid double-tap would fire two parallel POSTs and could claim two different permits; the isPending guard at SearchPermitsSheet.tsx:72 is the fence.
The claim body must use the canonical `${permit_num}--${revision_num}` lead_id; the earlier `permit-${a}-${b}` shape was never parsed server-side and silently claimed nothing.
Two distinct empty renders — "Type 2+ characters to search" below the threshold and "No permits found" above it (SearchPermitsSheet.tsx:145-155).
A failed claim renders an inline red block and is cleared when the sheet reopens, so a stale error is never shown on a fresh open.
Measured zero: the search field and every result row carry no accessibility attribute at all.

errors.why: A failed claim renders an inline red block above the results; a failed SEARCH renders nothing at all and looks like "No permits found".

classes.ui: Inline "Failed to claim job. Please try again."
Same inline claim error; a search 500 is invisible.
ZodError re-thrown to the root ErrorBoundary (useSearchPermits throwOnError).

emits.why: Claiming a job from search — the act the whole flight board exists for — emits no analytics event; only the DEV-only query_invalidate breadcrumb fires.

offers.why: No sponsored placement is rendered: the only slot component in the Expo tree is SponsorSlot, and it returns null unless EXPO_PUBLIC_PARCEL_SPONSORS=1.

metering.why: Nothing here is counted: the Spec 126 §7 usage ledger table does not exist (grep for usage_events in the introspected drizzle schema returns 0 hits), and the only quota-shaped counter, user_profiles.lead_views_count, is incremented solely by POST /api/leads/view, which has no mobile caller.

config.why: Its two tunables — the 2-character minimum and the 20-row LIMIT — are literals in the hook and the SQL, not registered logic variables, and there is no debounce at all.

sharing.why: GET /api/leads/search is exclusive to this sheet, but the claim POST is the same /api/leads/save contract the feed, the lead detail and the flight board all write through.

limitations.what: The search has no debounce and no rate limit: every keystroke past two characters issues a request the 60s cache may not cover, against a route with no withRateLimit.
limitations.measured: useSearchPermits.ts:16-24 fires on the raw query; src/app/api/leads/search/route.ts imports no rate-limit helper — unlike /api/leads/feed, /api/leads/save and /api/parcels/lookup.

limitations.what: A failed search is indistinguishable from an empty result.
limitations.measured: SearchPermitsSheet.tsx:29 destructures only { data, isFetching }; isError is never read.

notes: The parcel search screen debounces at 400ms against a 60/min bucket; this sheet, searching a much larger table, debounces not at all against no bucket. Both are SEARCH archetypes and the contrast is measured, not inferred.

programme.why: Permit data for the lead-gen product. Inventoried only; it converts under the same standard in a later programme.
